title: rx_thread re-enters lora_recv immediately on non-EAGAIN errors
description:
In lora_l2.c rx_thread() (lines 152-158), when lora_recv() returns a negative value other than -EAGAIN, the error is logged but the loop immediately retries without any delay.

Trigger: Persistent LoRa driver error (e.g., -EIO from misconfigured SPI, hardware failure, or driver bug).

Bad behavior: Tight retry loop floods logs with 'LoRa RX error: -X' messages at maximum rate, starving other threads (priority 7 is relatively high), and potentially masking the root cause in the log buffer. On battery-powered devices, this also drains power rapidly.

Consider: exponential backoff on repeated non-EAGAIN errors, or stopping after N consecutive failures.

Location: firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/lora_l2.c lines 152-158
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified, no further change needed. lora_l2.c rx_thread() (lines 432-470) no longer re-enters lora_recv() unconditionally on non-EAGAIN errors: it counts consecutive_errors, resets on -EAGAIN timeout and on any successful recv, logs LOG_ERR per error with a LOG_WRN summary every RX_ERROR_WARN_THRESHOLD (5) consecutive failures, and sleeps 1000ms before retrying - preventing the tight retry loop, log flooding, CPU starvation, and battery drain the bead describes. A later bead (i1gk.103) already reviewed the backoff-vs-join-timeout interaction. Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -std=c11 -Wall --target=armv7m-none-eabi on lora_l2.c with stub Zephyr headers and Kconfig-default -D flags: exit 0 (1 stub-artifact warning, see 9j70.30 close). CI gap: native_sim / pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 build not runnable locally.
